top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level adaptive aero control shell. Integrates firmware-visible CSR/MMIO, request transport, response validation, timeout/stale detection, bounded actuator command generation, and safe fallback behavior. It is the required top module and is fully synthesizable RTL.
top_module.functionality: Implements the digital control shell around a remote surrogate execution service. The module accepts packed 128-bit requests only when valid/ready handshakes complete, captures sequence/mode/reference/velocity summary/config tags, emits request context to the host side, accepts 128-bit responses from the host side, validates echoed sequence, freshness, and age, rejects stale or mismatched responses, latches timeout/fault conditions, and produces a bounded 64-bit actuator command or a safe fallback command. The module also exposes a small firmware-visible register window for mode control, sequence tracking, timeout/stale limits, actuator bounds, fallback selection, and fault clear semantics.
responsibilities: Accept and backpressure model requests until downstream acceptance conditions allow a new outstanding request.
Expose a 128-bit request record on s_req_data with valid/ready semantics to the remote software surrogate runner.
Accept a 128-bit response record on s_rsp_data with valid/ready semantics and validate sequence/freshness/age before use.
Generate a 64-bit actuator command word only from validated response data or from safe fallback manager state.
Clamp actuator target fields to programmable min/max bounds before issuing the command.
Assert safe fallback on reset, timeout expiry, stale response detection, invalid response status, or host fault conditions.
Provide firmware-visible CSR/MMIO access to operating mode, timeout limit, stale-age limit, actuator bounds, fallback selector, request sequence, status, and fault clear controls.
Use technology-neutral block RAM style storage for request/response history or buffering when needed for timing closure.
Keep all outputs registered and deterministic, with no combinational loops across ready/valid or control paths.
top_module.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, clear outstanding request state, clear validated-response state, clear timeout and stale counters, assert safe fallback, set command outputs to the predefined safe aerodynamic configuration, deassert command valid until a fresh valid response is accepted, and initialize MMIO status readback to faultless safe mode with explicit reset state fields as defined by the register contract.
behavior_rules: s_req_valid and s_req_data are only captured when s_req_ready is asserted in the same cycle.
At most one outstanding request is tracked for command generation unless internal buffering is explicitly enabled by the implementation using the declared memory macro.
s_rsp_valid data is accepted only when s_rsp_ready is asserted; accepted responses must echo the outstanding request sequence number.
Responses with mismatched sequence, invalid status, expired age, or after watchdog expiry are rejected and must not update m_cmd_data.
Timeout watchdog starts on request acceptance and expires after the programmable timeout limit; expiration latches fault status until cleared by MMIO fault-clear write or reset.
Stale-data detection independently rejects delayed responses using programmable stale-age limit and/or sequence progress.
Any fault, timeout, stale response, or host fault bit forces safe fallback command generation and suppresses normal actuator updates until release conditions are satisfied.
Actuator target fields in the command word are clipped to programmable min/max bounds, and clipping must be reflected in status.
Firmware writes that attempt illegal configuration values are ignored or flagged, but must not create unsafe control states.

The request and response transport direction contract is authoritative: request valid/data are outputs to the surrogate service, request ready is an input from the surrogate service; response valid/data are inputs from the surrogate service, response ready is an output to the surrogate service.
Top-level outputs must have real RTL drivers; no required top-level output may be left undriven or connected only through a child input.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_request_capture
modules.description: Captures and packs outgoing request metadata, tracks request sequence acceptance, and generates request-side context for the external surrogate service and internal monitoring. It also participates in outstanding-request tracking and history storage by writing request metadata into the declared block RAM style storage when enabled.
modules.functionality: Decodes the packed request record into explicit semantic fields used by downstream control and bookkeeping logic. When a request handshake completes, the module emits request sequence, operating mode, vehicle/geometry reference selector, velocity summary, and configuration tags. It also generates a one-cycle metadata-valid pulse and optional history write controls for the technology-neutral RAM wrapper. The module does not generate actuator commands and does not accept responses.
responsibilities: Decode packed 128-bit request records into explicit semantic request fields.
Generate request-side capture status for one outstanding request at a time.
Provide write controls for request history storage when a request is accepted.
Backpressure incoming request traffic when the controller is busy or when fault suppression requires it.
Preserve request sequence and metadata until the request is retired or superseded by a reset.
modules.reset_behavior: Drive s_req_ready low only until the controller is able to accept a request, clear captured request fields, deassert req_meta_valid, and place history write controls inactive under reset.
behavior_rules: s_req_data is sampled only when s_req_valid and s_req_ready are both asserted.
The request fields are explicit semantic outputs and must remain stable until a new accepted request or reset.
History write controls are only asserted on accepted request events and must target the declared RAM wrapper storage path.
This module does not infer or fabricate responses; response handling is external to its scope.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_response_validate
modules.description: Validates incoming surrogate responses against the outstanding request sequence and freshness constraints, detects stale or timed-out responses, and produces sanitized response result fields for command generation. It may read request history from the declared memory macro when enabled to cross-check context.
modules.functionality: Consumes a packed response record, checks echoed sequence number against the outstanding request sequence, examines freshness/age/status fields, and produces validated control-result summary fields only when the response is eligible for actuation. Rejected, stale, or timed-out responses are flagged and prevented from updating downstream command generation. The module can read request history through the block RAM wrapper if needed for verification or context retrieval.
responsibilities: Accept only responses that match the current outstanding request sequence.
Reject responses that are stale, expired by watchdog, or indicate invalid status.
Produce sanitized response summary fields for downstream command generation.
Provide explicit validated and rejected strobes for control/status aggregation.
Use the declared memory macro interface when request history lookup is required.
modules.reset_behavior: Deassert readiness only when the controller is not able to accept a response, clear validation outputs, clear rejection pulses, and drive the RAM wrapper controls inactive under reset.
behavior_rules: s_rsp_data is sampled only when s_rsp_valid and s_rsp_ready are both asserted.
Response sequence mismatch, invalid status, timeout expiration, or stale limit hit causes rsp_rejected and prevents rsp_validated from asserting.
Validated responses must preserve echoed sequence, freshness tag, status, and compact control result summary in explicit semantic ports.
No response may update actuator outputs unless rsp_validated is asserted in the same transaction flow.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_timeout_watchdog
modules.description: Tracks outstanding request age and generates timeout and stale-data indicators under programmable limits. It latches fault events until cleared by the controller and provides deterministic, cycle-based expiry behavior.
modules.functionality: Starts timing on request acceptance, increments age while a request remains outstanding, and asserts timeout_expired when the programmable cycle limit is reached without a validated matching response. Independently evaluates stale_age_limit to reject delayed responses and latches fault conditions until cleared. The module does not generate actuator commands and does not decode transport payloads.
responsibilities: Implement cycle-based watchdog timing for outstanding requests.
Assert timeout_expired deterministically when the programmable limit elapses.
Assert stale_limit_hit when request/response age exceeds the programmable stale-age limit.
Latch fault state until explicit software clear or reset.
Provide age/status outputs for controller aggregation and MMIO status readback.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset age counters to zero, deassert timeout and stale indicators, and clear latched fault state into safe fallback on rst_n deassertion.
behavior_rules: Age counting begins only when a request is accepted.
Validated response acceptance clears the active watchdog condition for the current request, but latched fault conditions remain set until cleared.
Timeout and stale indicators are separate outputs and may assert independently.
The stale detector is not allowed to silently modify command outputs; it only informs controller suppression and faulting.
Programmable limits of zero are legal only if explicitly interpreted by the controller as immediate expiry or disabled behavior per MMIO contract; unsafe ambiguity must be avoided in implementation.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_command_manager
modules.description: Generates the 64-bit actuator command word from validated response data or from safe fallback state, applies programmable clamps, encodes enable/fallback state, and produces a bounded command suitable for downstream actuator control.
modules.functionality: Consumes only validated response summary fields or safe fallback state, constructs a compact actuator command word, clamps every actuator target field to programmed minimum and maximum bounds, and encodes enable/fallback state plus optional parity/checksum intent. The module ensures the command is bounded and deterministic and never forwards unvalidated response data directly to the actuator bus.
responsibilities: Generate 64-bit actuator command words only from validated response inputs or fallback state.
Enforce programmable lower and upper bounds on every actuator target field.
Assert clipped status when any field is limited by clamp logic.
Drive a safe predetermined configuration when fallback_active is asserted.
Register command outputs and obey actuator ready backpressure semantics.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, drive the actuator command bus to the predefined safe aerodynamic configuration, deassert command valid until a legal command is available, and clear clipping and validation indicators.
behavior_rules: If fallback_active is asserted, the generated command must reflect the safe fallback configuration regardless of response inputs.
Every commanded actuator target must be clipped to the programmed bounds before being placed on m_cmd_data.
Validated responses may update the actuator command only when rsp_validated is asserted and no fault suppression is active.
The command word must remain bounded and deterministic across backpressure cycles.
No large payloads or model artifacts may be embedded in the command word.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_csr_mmio
modules.description: Firmware-visible small control/status register block that exposes operating mode, sequence counter, timeout/stale limits, actuator bounds, fallback selector, fault clear, and status readback for the adaptive aero control shell. It decodes a compact 32-bit MMIO window and produces explicit semantic control outputs.
modules.functionality: Implements a small software-visible control-plane register window with decode for a compact set of configuration and status registers only. It translates MMIO reads and writes into explicit semantic control outputs used by the top-level controller and returns status fields and the current watchdog age on reads. It never stores bulk payloads and never exposes inaccessible internal state as software-visible.
responsibilities: Decode MMIO transactions for operating mode, sequence counter, timeout limit, stale-age limit, actuator bounds, fallback selector, and fault clear semantics.
Provide readback of fault, fallback, request pending, validated-response, and watchdog age status fields.
Ignore or flag invalid writes to reserved or out-of-range address regions without creating unsafe control states.
Present a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, transaction-valid/write-enable, and response/ready semantics.
Ensure every declared register is reachable through RTL decode and no declared software-visible register remains inaccessible.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset all configuration outputs to conservative safe values, clear fault-clear strobes, drive mmio_ready inactive until transactions are accepted, and return read data corresponding to reset-safe status and configuration defaults.
behavior_rules: MMIO writes modify only the documented register fields and must not be used for bulk storage.
Each declared register field must be reachable through decode and readable or writable as documented.
Out-of-range or illegal configuration writes must be ignored or flagged, never propagated into unsafe states.
Fault clear is a pulse-like control output intended to clear latched timeout/stale fault conditions in the watchdog and top-level controller.
The MMIO block may not substitute for streaming transport and may not carry model payloads or geometry arrays.
Register contract values are the authoritative firmware-visible behavior.

top_level_connections.description: Distribute the single synchronous clock to all submodules.
Fan out the active-low synchronous reset to all submodules.
Outgoing model-request valid from the system request ingress into request capture and transport logic.
Model-request ready returned from request capture/availability control to the top-level request ingress.
Packed 128-bit request record captured from the top-level request ingress.
Incoming model-response valid from the external surrogate service into response validation logic.
Model-response ready driven by response validation/control back to the external surrogate service.
Packed 128-bit response record from the external surrogate service into response validation logic.
Top-level actuator command valid driven by command manager.
Actuator-side ready input delivered to command manager.
Bounded 64-bit actuator command word driven by command manager.
Firmware-visible MMIO transaction-valid input into CSR block.
Firmware-visible MMIO write-enable input into CSR block.
Firmware-visible MMIO address bus into CSR block.
Firmware-visible MMIO write-data bus into CSR block.
Firmware-visible MMIO read-data output driven by CSR block.
Firmware-visible MMIO response/ready output driven by CSR block.

inter_module_signals.name: req_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Outstanding request sequence number forwarded to response validation for echo matching.

inter_module_signals.name: req_meta_valid
inter_module_signals.description: Accepted request event used to start the watchdog and outstanding-request timing.

inter_module_signals.name: rsp_status
inter_module_signals.description: Validated response status forwarded to command generation.

inter_module_signals.name: rsp_control_result
inter_module_signals.description: Compact validated control result summary forwarded to command manager.

inter_module_signals.name: rsp_validated
inter_module_signals.description: Validated-response event distributed to watchdog, command manager, and status reporting.

inter_module_signals.name: timeout_limit
inter_module_signals.description: Programmable timeout limit from firmware to watchdog.

inter_module_signals.name: stale_age_limit
inter_module_signals.description: Programmable stale-age limit from firmware to watchdog.

inter_module_signals.name: act_min
inter_module_signals.description: Programmable lower actuator bound from firmware to command manager.

inter_module_signals.name: act_max
inter_module_signals.description: Programmable upper actuator bound from firmware to command manager.

inter_module_signals.name: cfg_fault_clear
inter_module_signals.description: Dedicated software clear pulse to release latched timeout and stale faults.

inter_module_signals.name: fault_latched
inter_module_signals.description: Latched fault indication reported to the CSR/MMIO block and top-level status output.

inter_module_signals.name: timeout_expired
inter_module_signals.description: Watchdog timeout indication delivered to response validation for rejection of late responses.

inter_module_signals.name: stale_limit_hit
inter_module_signals.description: Stale-data detection indicator delivered to response validation for response rejection.

inter_module_signals.name: watchdog_age
inter_module_signals.description: Current watchdog age presented to the CSR/MMIO block for firmware readback.

inter_module_signals.name: fallback_active
inter_module_signals.description: Fallback activation derived from latched fault state and distributed to command manager and status reporting.

inter_module_signals.name: cmd_validated
inter_module_signals.description: Command-valid state used to indicate that a non-fallback command has been produced for a pending request.

registers.name: CTRL
registers.description: Control register containing operating mode and fallback selection fields.

fields.name: fault_clear
fields.description: Write-one pulse to clear latched timeout/stale faults.

registers.name: SEQ
registers.description: Sequence counter tracking the host/software request ordering.

fields.name: seq_counter
fields.description: Request sequence counter visible to firmware.

fields.name: stale_age_limit
fields.description: Maximum acceptable response age in cycles.

registers.name: STATUS
registers.description: Status register returning fault and activity state.
